objectives_fil: Maipapaliwanag ng BHW ang legal na batayan ng kanyang tungkulin ayon sa RA 7883, at matutukoy niya kung sino ang nagbibigay ng akreditasyon bago siya opisyal na makapagsimula sa gawain.
Maililista ng BHW ang mga benepisyong maaari niyang matanggap sa ilalim ng RA 7883, at matutukoy niya kung ano ang kailangan bago siya maging eligible dito.
Maipapaliwanag ng BHW ang mga kondisyon ng BHW Eligibility (BHWE) sa Civil Service, at masusuri niya kung siya ay kwalipikado na o hindi pa.
Makapagpapakita ang BHW ng kalmado at matiyagang pag-uugali kapag humaharap sa mabagal na proseso ng rehistrasyon o pag-follow-up sa isang benepisyong dapat niyang matanggap.
objectives_en: The BHW can explain the legal basis of their role under RA 7883, and identify who accredits a BHW before they can officially begin their work.
The BHW can list the benefits available to them under RA 7883, and identify what is required before they are eligible for these.
The BHW can explain the conditions for BHW Eligibility (BHWE) in the Civil Service, and assess whether they are already qualified or not yet.
The BHW can demonstrate calm, patient behavior when facing a slow registration process or when following up on a benefit they are owed.
summary_fil: May legal na batayan ang tungkulin ng BHW — hindi lang ito kabaitang boluntaryo. Ayon sa RA 7883, ang BHW ay opisyal na kinikilala matapos ang akreditasyon ng local health board, at kasama sa batas na iyon ang mga benepisyong dapat niyang matanggap: hazard allowance, subsistence allowance, pagsasanay, civil service eligibility, libreng legal services, at priority sa mga pautang. Ang BHW Eligibility sa Civil Service ay may sariling kondisyon — akreditado, may dalawang taon sa kolehiyo, limang taon nang tuloy-tuloy na naglilingkod, at may satisfactory service. Alam man ang lahat ng ito, mabagal pa rin minsan ang proseso — at doon pumapasok ang huling bahagi ng modyul na ito: ang kakayahang maghintay nang matiyaga at humingi ng nararapat nang may kumpiyansa, hindi may sama ng loob at hindi rin tahimik na lang sumusuko.
summary_en: A BHW's duty has a legal basis — it is not only voluntary kindness. Under RA 7883, a BHW is officially recognized after accreditation by the local health board, and that same law carries the benefits they are owed: hazard allowance, subsistence allowance, training, civil service eligibility, free legal services, and priority access to loans. BHW Eligibility in the Civil Service has its own conditions — accredited, at least two years of college, five years of continuous service, and a satisfactory record. Knowing all of this still doesn't make the process fast — and that's where this module's last part comes in: the skill of waiting with patience and asking for what's owed with confidence, without resentment and without quietly giving up.
